broader_coverage.reasoning: ℓ1 is not reflexive. With unbounded exponents, choose a subsequence with p_{n_k}≥k: its indicator is in the full Nakano target but has tail norm bounded below by one, proving target non-order-continuity. The 2022 stated essential-norm theorem and bounded-exponent compactness corollary therefore do not imply this quantitative unbounded-exponent classification. For bounded exponent sequences the present result becomes the standard noncompact value one, and does not seek novelty there.

originality.rationale: Checked actual published records and read the closest three accessible primary sources in detail. Existing qualitative Nakano noncompactness does not quantify the compact distance; the closest general multiplier essential-norm theorem requires properties absent here, and the recent modular embedding article treats a different bounded-exponent compactness situation. Targeted searches for exact threshold, equivalent finite-cover/approximation formulations and broader claims found no dominating match. Priority remains tentative for older nonseparable modular-space literature.
residual_risks: Older general theorems on measures of noncompactness of unit-vector inclusions in nonseparable Köthe lattices could yield an equivalent statement under different language.
Publication priority is based on inspected accessible primary sources and a bounded published-record search; no exhaustive independent historical review has been performed.

value.rationale: Quantitative completion of a motivated natural embedding problem: exact compact distance, complete limiting approximation-number profile and Hausdorff noncompactness radius, plus a sharp logarithmic growth phase. The invariant is intrinsic to an infinite modular exponent sequence and distinguishes full nonorder-continuous targets from cases covered by earlier methods. Not an arbitrary finite truncation or simple normalization check.
